title: FlexHiNM-GP: Flexible Hierarchical Pruning via Region Allocation and Channel Permutation
claim: Fixed-ratio pruning schemes leave importance unevenly matched to sparsity; flexible, permuted, multi-region allocation aligns sparsity levels with sorted importance.
layout: 4 panels in a row, left-to-right, annotated curves with dashed region dividers
description: A single row of four small line plots, labeled (a) HiNM, (b) HiNM-P, (c) FlexHiNM and (d) FlexHiNM-P. Each plot has the x-axis 'Sorted column vectors' and the y-axis 'Ratio of important elements (R)', which runs from 0 to 1. A curve falls from left to right in each panel. The curves are black, blue, purple and red. Dashed vertical lines divide each plot into regions. Red labels in each region give the sparsity pattern: 2:4 (mma.sp), 0:4, or 4:4 (mma) for the dense region. Cyan callout boxes give the range of R for each region, for example 0.4<R<1 or R<0.25. HiNM has two regions. The permuted variant has a sharper step. The Flex variants have three regions, with a dense region added. The red panel (d) shows the clearest step shapes.
caption: HiNM variants
abstract: N:M sparsity has emerged as a hardware-friendly pruning strategy, notably supported by NVIDIA’s Sparse Tensor Cores. While efficient, its fixed sparsity ratio restricts flexibility, making it difficult to adapt pruning granularity to varying weight importance across layers and architectures. To overcome this limitation, we propose FlexHiNM, a hybrid framework that adaptively partitions each layer into three regions: dense, vector-pruned, and N:M sparse, enabling finer-grained control while preserving hardware compatibility. To better preserve salient weights, we extend this to FlexHiNM-GP, which incorporates Gyro-Permutation, an iterative channel-rearrangement algorithm. Through successive sampling, clustering, and assignment, Gyro-Permutation aligns high-importance weights with structured sparsity patterns and mitigates suboptimal configurations in multi-level pruning. During gradual pruning, FlexHiNM-GP further employs a differentiable masking mechanism based on the Hard Concrete distribution, enabling gradient-based mask learning and preventing over-aggressive early pruning. Experiments on vision and language benchmarks demonstrate that FlexHiNM-GP consistently surpasses strong structured baselines and approaches the performance of unstructured pruning, validating the effectiveness of combining hybrid sparsity with learned masks and permutation strategies.
